newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares strolled to their fifth consecutive closing high on Monday after a moderately brisk but unremarkable session.
"It wasn't a big news day," a dealer said. "Volumes were slightly higher than usual for a Monday, but overall there was not much happening."
The AEX blue chip index ended five points or 0.65 percent higher at a new record close of 769.96 after briefly peaking at a new all-time intra-day high of 772.76 points.
Dealers said profit takers stepped in late in the session as Wall Street opened range-bound and hi-tech stocks saw pressure.
"We've seen some profit-taking this afternoon after Wall Street opened and took some heat out of the market," one trader said.
Philips was a prime target for investors looking to take profits, falling 2.10 guilders to 88.70.

News of a 0.5 percent point hike in the Dutch secured loans rate -- the equivalent of Germany's discount rate -- to 2.50 percent, and a fresh increase in the secured loans rate to 2.90 percent, had little impact as an increase had already been largely factored in, dealers said.

Trade in Dutch PTT was brisk ahead of the company's 1996 results due out on Tuesday. The stock topped the volume charts for the entire session, closing up 3.10 guilders or 4.6 percent at 70.20 guilders.
"There is a lot of speculation in the stock," a trader said. "Many players are also buying in order to cover call options."
Software house CMG booked a strong early rise after sharply higher 1996 earnings and an upbeat forecast.
The shares later pared gains to close 0.70 guilders up at a new closing high for the year of 38.20, off the session peak of 39.00 guilders.
